Welcome to Graduately Developing Futures....OFSTED rated GOOD in all areas
Graduately Developing Futures Pride & Vision
Graduately Developing Futures Mission
To engage those who are disengaged, isolated, hard to reach, disadvantaged and who have Special Educational Needs in learning interventions that will develop confidence, self-esteem, resilience and skills and experiences needed to embrace life-long learning, utilising our outdoor learning environment to provide real life experiences.
Engage Motivate Inspire
EMI is our ethos and we are able to achieve this through our environment at Valley View Farm, its personnel, relationship bonding and trust with parents guardians and foster parents.
Graduately Developing Futures - Achieving the Mission
Graduately Developing Future (GDF)'s curriculum reflects the particular needs of those with Special Educational Needs (SEN) and Education Health Care Plans (EHCP). GDF caters for and engages with students from right across the spectrum and works in partnership with local authorities across Dorset to ensure it meets identified gaps in local provision. GDF’s outdoor learning environment provides the opportunity for utilising real life experiences and taking a kinaesthetic approach.
We consider provision of a complete educational context, from ages 6 to 14, which allows the most effective route through which students can be motivated and inspired to fulfil their individual educational and social potential.
Children and young people with SEN can have their learning needs characterised
by the triad of impairments listed below:
· Difficulties in communication – both receptive and expressive
· Difficulties in forming effective social relationships
· Impairment of imagination and flexibility of thought
Students attending GDF may also experience extreme anxiety and have low self-esteem. Coping with daily life can be extremely arduous, GDF is dedicated to mitigating such difficulties thereby increasing the students learning receptivity, attainment
and life skill base.

Schools play an essential role in protecting children from harm. They have
regular contact with children and young people so are in a strong
position to identify signs of abuse and neglect.
Our school safeguards children by:
robust safeguarding practices
keep-up-to-date with policy and practice
don’t pose a risk to children
any member of staff if they have a worry or problem

Engage Motivate Inspire
Improved socialising skills - he calls them friends
I just thought I would send an email to you to thank you from the bottom of my heart for all your hard work and dedication that you and your staff have shown towards J over the last 2 years .
When J first came to the farm he was literally a broken shell regarding his previous education or lack of. When he came to you he couldn’t write his name had no literacy or numeracy skills and was lead to believe he was just a disrespectful little boy who refused to learn anything.
You all showed him so much patience and respect which helped J to learn to both trust and respect his peers. Which lead him to believe in himself and his ability to start to learn.
Within a few weeks J had gained so much in all aspects of learning , respect and wiliness to engage in pretty much anything .
Having the animals there also helped J by measuring their food to ensure they were getting the right amount so J was using his numeracy skills without realizing it, totally brilliant. J also enjoys the cooking sessions and is so pleased with himself when he comes home with food that he’s help to make and explains to me what has gone into it and how it was cooked.
I have seen my Grandson go from a very confused, withdrawn, angry and troubled little boy, to a happy, confident, settled, calm, little boy who now wants to engage in learning and willingness to help others .
Once again I want to thank you all for what you and your staff have done to help J grow into this confident little boy, who’s now engaging in education and enjoying his learning .
Learn more about how we can help....
Engage Motivate Inspire
Thanks again for such a positive experience
M has definitely come out of his shell more since having a placement at the farm school. He loves the practical aspects of it and has come home, majority of the time in a much happier mood albeit some days, mentally tired as a result. He also has improved with his socialising skills there with the other students to the point he calls them friends. This has also had a positive impact with him. If all schools had this approach I feel children would have a much happier experience of school. Many thanks for all your current hard work as well as your team.
